q: Different types of sand serve specialized roles in construction, ranging from general filling to structural reinforcement. While some sands focus on stability, others are processed to achieve fine texture and high density, making them ideal for plastering, levelling and masonry applications. Which type of sand undergoes a screening process to ensure consistency in grain size and improved workability for finishing tasks?
n: Vibrasand is a screened (vibro-sieved) sand with consistent grain size and good workability for plastering, leveling and masonry finishing. Source: Local aggregate product classification; ASTM C144 (aggregate for masonry mortar).

q: A stockpile of uniformly graded construction sand is dumped on a level surface during site preparation. Assuming the material is dry, free-flowing, and not influenced by confinement or moisture-induced cohesion, what is the most realistic angle of repose governing the natural slope of the pile?
o: 18° NOTE: Angle of Repose is a RANGE, not a specific value
n: Dry, free-flowing sand rests at about 30°–35°, so 35° is the most realistic value given. The angle of repose is really a range. Source: Das, Principles of Geotechnical Engineering, Ch. 12.

q: An artificial stone made by mixing cement, aggregates and water is ___ concrete.
n: Plain concrete is the artificial stone made by mixing cement, aggregates and water, without reinforcement. Source: PCA, Design and Control of Concrete Mixtures, Ch. 1; NSCP 2015, Sec. 414 (Plain Concrete).

q: Standard rebar for CHB Jaying
n: 10 mm deformed bars are standard for CHB wall reinforcement in local residential work. Source: DPWH Standard Specifications, Item 1046 (Masonry Works); NBC IRR Rule VIII (Group A dwellings).

q: Standard rebar length
n: Rebars are commercially sold in standard lengths of 6.0, 7.5, 9.0, 10.5 and 12.0 m. Source: PNS 49 (Steel Bars for Concrete Reinforcement).

q: Standard angle bar length
n: Structural angle bars are commonly stocked in 6.0 m lengths. Source: PNS 657 / local steel product catalogs.

q: A short steel bar extending from one concrete element to another, placed in preparation for the next concreting works.
n: A dowel is a short bar extending from one concrete element into the next pour, so the two are tied together. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated; NSCP 2015, Sec. 416.3 (dowels).

q: What is the most common nominal diameter for schedule 40 GI pipes used in scaffolding in the Philippines?
n: Local scaffolding commonly uses 1½-inch (48.3 mm OD) Schedule 40 GI pipe. Source: DOLE OSHS Rule 1414 (Scaffolding); BS EN 39 (scaffold tubes, 48.3 mm OD).

q: Which is NOT a raw material for-rebar spacer?
n: Rebar spacers (chairs) are made of concrete, metal or plastic. Foam is too compressible. Source: ACI 315 / CRSI Manual of Standard Practice (bar supports).

q: A mid-rise commercial building is preparing for the concreting of its heavily loaded structural members, including columns and major beams. The structural notes specify the use of Class AA concrete, which is required for elements that must achieve higher compressive strength and durability. During the pre-pour briefing, the site supervisor asks the crew to confirm the correct proportion of cement, sand, and gravel for Class AA, since using the wrong ratio would compromise the strength of the structural frame. Which mixture ratio corresponds to Class AA concrete under Philippine construction practice?
n: Class AA concrete uses a 1:1.5:3 (cement:sand:gravel) mix for heavily loaded members. Source: DPWH Standard Specifications, Item 405 (Classes of Concrete).

q: What comprises 60% to 80% of a typical concrete mix to reduce cost?
n: Aggregates make up about 60–80% of concrete volume, the cheap filler that also gives stability. Source: PCA, Design and Control of Concrete Mixtures, Ch. 1 and 5.

q: A crew in Quezon City is batching concrete using a 1-bagger mixer for a suspended slab pour. To avoid cement balling, ensure proper coating of aggregates, and maintain uniform workability, the foreman instructs the helper to load the dry materials in the correct sequence before adding the remaining water. Which of the following orders reflects the proper placement of materials into the mixer?
n: Dry materials are usually loaded gravel first, then sand, then cement. The coarse aggregate scours the drum and the cement coats the aggregates evenly without balling. Source: PCA, Design and Control of Concrete Mixtures (mixing practice); DPWH Item 405.

q: Term used to level a lot/land, thereby ensuring a stable base for construction works
n: Grading levels and shapes the land to a stable, properly sloped base for construction. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (site work).

q: Soil treatment prior to slab concrete pouring.
n: Soil poisoning (anti-termite treatment) is applied to the ground before the slab is poured. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated; DPWH Item 1100 (soil poisoning).

q: How soon can you step on newly poured concrete?
n: Light foot traffic is generally allowed on new concrete after about 1–2 days. Source: PCA, Design and Control of Concrete Mixtures, Ch. 12; ACI 302.1R.

q: Durability and strength improve in concrete mix when the water-cement ratio is?
n: A lower water-cement ratio gives stronger, denser, more durable concrete. Source: PCA, Design and Control of Concrete Mixtures, Ch. 9 (Abrams' law).

q: A kind of form which can be left behind after concrete pouring and becomes integral to the building structure. If properly designed, it can lead to thinner slabs thereby resulting to substantial savings both in laber and material cost.
n: Steel deck (metal decking) is a stay-in-place form that becomes part of the composite slab, allowing thinner slabs and saving labor and materials. Source: SDI Composite Steel Floor Deck Manual; Ching, Building Construction Illustrated.

q: Which among the following cement type has a property of rapid hardening aad very high rate of strength development? This cannot be used mass concreting works.
n: High-alumina cement hardens rapidly and gains strength very fast. Its high heat makes it unsuitable for mass concrete. Source: Neville, Properties of Concrete, Ch. 2.

q: Which cement type has slow hardening characteristics?
n: Portland pozzolana cement hardens slowly but gains strength over a long period. Source: Neville, Properties of Concrete, Ch. 2.

q: Which is a Philippine supplier of Portland cement?
n: Holcim (Holcim Philippines) makes Portland cement. Mariwasa is tiles, Puyat is steel and Universal is not a cement brand. Source: Manufacturer product lines.

q: Which type of joint is intentionally placed within a concrete structure to accommodate staged pours, ensuring continuity without compromising structural integrity?
n: A construction joint is placed where one pour stops and the next begins, keeping structural continuity. Source: ACI 224.3R (Joints in Concrete Construction); NSCP 2015, Sec. 426.5.6.

q: Which type of joint is intentionally created in a concrete slab or masonry wall to control the location of shrinkage cracks and maintain an orderly appearance?
n: Control (contraction) joints make weakened planes, so shrinkage cracks form along them in an orderly way. Source: ACI 224.3R.

q: Which type of joint completely separates a concrete element from adjoining structures to accommodate independent movement and reduce stress transfer?
n: Isolation joints fully separate an element from adjoining structures so each can move independently. Source: ACI 224.3R.

q: Which type of joint is provided in concrete construction to accommodate expansion and contraction caused by temperature changes?
n: Expansion joints are planned gaps through a structure or slab. They let the parts move as they expand and contract with temperature, so cracking does not occur. Source: ACI 224.3R (Joints in Concrete Construction).

q: When using control joints for slab on grade, what is the depth of cut for a 4-inch thick concrete slab?
n: Control joints are sawn to about one-quarter of the slab depth: 1 in. for a 4 in. slab. Source: ACI 302.1R / ACI 360R (joint depth = ¼ slab thickness).

q: What is the most common material used to cover floor expansion joints which is usually pre-formed?
n: Floor expansion joints are usually covered with preformed metal cover plates. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (expansion joint covers).

q: A building inspector observes water intrusion at the junction between a metal roof and a vertical wall. Which component should be installed to weatherproof the joint and prevent rainwater penetration?
n: Flashing seals the joint between a metal roof and a vertical wall against rain. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (flashing); NRCA Roofing Manual.

q: A below-grade foundation wall is exposed to continuous groundwater and must resist positive hydrostatic pressure. The specification requires a treatment capable of preventing active water infiltration, not just moisture migration. Which type of proofing is appropriate for this condition?
n: Groundwater under positive hydrostatic pressure needs true waterproofing. Dampproofing only resists moisture without pressure. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (waterproofing and dampproofing); NRCA Waterproofing Manual.

q: Xypex is a trusted brand in waterproofing, with products known to resist hydrostatic pressure, permanently seal hairline cracks, reactivate and self-heal, and provide chemical resistance. To which category of waterproofing does Xypex belong?
n: Xypex is a crystalline waterproofing system. Its chemicals grow crystals in the concrete pores that seal hairline cracks and reactivate (self-heal) when water returns. Source: Xypex product literature; ACI 212.3R (permeability-reducing admixtures).

q: A below-grade masonry wall exhibits moisture seepage due to hydrostatic pressure from adjacent soil. "The architect specifies a cement-based waterproofing compound that must be brush-applied directly onto damp masonry, capable of forming a crystalline barrier that integrates with the substrate rather than acting as a surface membrane. Which material best satisfies this performance requirement?
n: Thoroseal is a cement-based coating brushed onto damp masonry. It bonds into the substrate rather than acting as a surface membrane. Source: Thoroseal product literature; Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (waterproofing and dampproofing); NRCA Waterproofing Manual.

q: Which product is cementitious and is thus NOT an elastomeric waterproofing brand'?
n: Thoroseal is a cementitious waterproof coating applied like a slurry over masonry and concrete. It is rigid, so it is not an elastomeric (rubber-like, crack-bridging) membrane. Source: Manufacturer product literature.

q: When it comes to protecting concrete against saltwater, especially for structures near the sea, choosing the right waterproofing solution is crucial. Which among the following would you recommend?
n: Crystalline waterproofing becomes part of the concrete matrix and resists chlorides and saltwater, which suits marine structures. Source: ACI 212.3R; Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (waterproofing and dampproofing); NRCA Waterproofing Manual.

q: Which waterproofing is added together with the concrete mix?
n: Integral waterproofing is an admixture mixed into the concrete itself to reduce permeability. It is not a coating or membrane applied to the surface afterward. Source: ACI 212.3R (Chemical Admixtures for Concrete).

q: Which waterproofing is best for structure over bodies of water and in highly corrosive environment?
n: Crystalline systems seal the concrete itself and resist aggressive chemicals, which suits structures over water and corrosive environments. Source: ACI 212.3R.

q: During the waterproofing of a below-grade concrete wall, the architect specifies a material that provides automatic stoppage of water infiltration by swelling when exposed to moisture. The product must be capable of forming a sell-sealing barrier because it expands significantly upon hydration, allowing it to fill cracks and construction joints without relying on surface adhesion. Which material best meets this performance requirement?
n: Bentonite clay swells greatly when wet, forming a self-sealing barrier that fills cracks and joints. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (waterproofing and dampproofing); NRCA Waterproofing Manual (bentonite waterproofing).

q: What waterproofing is very common, is semi-flexible or rigid, and is NOT exposed to weathering or sunlight?
n: Cementitious waterproofing is very common. It is rigid or semi-flexible and used where it is not exposed to sun or weathering, as under tiles and in tanks. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (waterproofing and dampproofing); NRCA Waterproofing Manual.

q: A waterproofing method that uses flexible asphalt layers
n: Bituminous waterproofing uses flexible asphalt layers. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (waterproofing and dampproofing); NRCA Waterproofing Manual.

q: Waterproofing that utilizes synthetic rubber single layer flexible membrane
n: EPDM is a single-ply synthetic rubber membrane. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (waterproofing and dampproofing); NRCA Waterproofing Manual; NRCA Roofing Manual.

q: A tiled roofing system requires a waterproof layer beneath the roof tiles to prevent water intrusion caused by wind-driven rain and minor tile displacement. Which membrane is roast commonly used for this application?
n: Bituminous underlayment membranes are most commonly used beneath roof tiles. Source: NRCA Roofing Manual (tile roof underlayment).

q: A construction crew is preparing a roof deck for waterproofing. The specification calls for a system whose underside is heated until it liquefied, allowing it to fuse to the concrete substrate and form a continuous waterproof layer. Which waterproofing category does this system belong to?
n: Torch-on bituminous membranes are heated on the underside until molten, then fused to the substrate. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (waterproofing and dampproofing); NRCA Waterproofing Manual.

q: A waterproofing membrane ts being installed on a roof deck. Which tool is used to heat the underside of the membrane so it bonds to the substrate?
n: Torch-applied membranes are heated with a gas (propane) torch. Source: NRCA Roofing Manual (torch-applied systems).

q: An architect is designing a residential building on a site with normal soil moisture conditions and no significant hydrostatic pressure. To prevent moisture from rising through walls and floors by capillary action, a protective treatment is specified at the building envelope. Which system is most appropriate for this condition?
n: With normal soil moisture and no hydrostatic pressure, dampproofing is enough to stop capillary moisture. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (waterproofing and dampproofing); NRCA Waterproofing Manual.

q: Which is an affordable damp-proofing membrane laid under a concrete slab on grade to prevent the concrete from gaining moisture through capillary action?
n: Polyethylene sheet is the low-cost vapor and damp-proof membrane laid under slabs on grade. Source: ACI 302.1R (vapor retarders); Ching, Building Construction Illustrated.

q: An architect is supervising the construction of a 12-storey residential tower in Mandaluyong. During inspection of the toilet and bath areas on multiple floors, he notes that the substrate is newly cast reinforced concrete with integral floor drains, cold joints at wall-to-slab intersections, and pipe penetrations for water closets and lavatories. The area will be fully tiled afterward, and the developer requires a waterproofing system that bonds strongly to concrete, is compatible with tile adhesives, can withstand constant moisture exposure, and does not rely on UV resistance since it will be covered. Which waterproofing system is most appropriate for this application?
n: Wet areas to be tiled suit cementitious waterproofing. It bonds well to concrete, works with tile adhesives, tolerates constant moisture and needs no UV resistance. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (waterproofing and dampproofing); NRCA Waterproofing Manual; ANSI A118.10.

q: Anarchitect is evaluating water-ingress issues on the exterior facade of a mid-rise office building in Ortigas. The facade consists of painted reinforced concrete walls with numerous hairline cracks caused by thermal cycling. The building is fully exposed to sun and rain, and the owner wants a waterproofing system that can bridge hairline cracks. resist UV degradation, remain flexible under daily expansion and contraction. and serve as both a protective and decorative coating. No soil backfill, ponding water. or tile topping are involved. Which waterproofing system is most appropriate for this facade application?
n: An elastomeric coating bridges hairline cracks, resists UV and stays flexible, while also serving as a decorative finish. Source: ASTM D6904; Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (waterproofing and dampproofing); NRCA Waterproofing Manual.

q: How do you prevent the entry of soil into perforated drainage pipes when installed at the basement?
o: Attach pumps to suck out the soil
n: Wrapping perforated drain pipe in geotextile filter fabric keeps soil out while letting water in. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (waterproofing and dampproofing); NRCA Waterproofing Manual (foundation drainage); ASTM D6707.

q: Which of the following metal combinations cannot be used together in direct contact on a roofing system due to accelerated deterioration of one material over time?
n: Aluminum touching copper causes severe galvanic corrosion. The aluminum is eaten away. Source: NRCA Roofing Manual (galvanic compatibility); ASTM G82.

q: A truss without vertical members that uses only the diagonals to carry loads.
n: A Warren truss has no verticals. Its diagonals alternate in tension and compression. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (truss types).

q: Which modern roof truss connection method uses galvanized steel plates with punched teeth that are hydraulically pressed into timber joints, providing fast, uniform, and high-strength assembly in prefabricated systems?
o: Gang Nail Be gy fan Q 'd
n: Gang-nail (toothed metal connector) plates are hydraulically pressed into timber joints to assemble prefabricated trusses. Source: TPI 1 (truss plate design); Ching, Building Construction Illustrated.
